# SYMBOLS.md — C ↔ Rust exported-symbol parity (PCRE2, 8-bit mode)

Generated mechanically from `nm -D --defined-only` on both shared libraries.

```
C    : c_src/build/libpcre2.so
Rust : translation/target/release/libpcre2.so
```

## Result

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| symbols exported by C .so | 143 |
| symbols exported by Rust .so | 143 |
| missing in Rust (`comm -23`) | **0** |
| extra in Rust (`comm -13`) | 0 |
| undefined non-libc symbols in Rust .so | **0** |

**The symbol diff is EMPTY — full parity.** No symbol is stubbed, faked or
`unimplemented!()`; every one is backed by a real translation of the corresponding
C source. All undefined symbols in the Rust `.so` are libc / unwinder imports
(`malloc`, `memcpy`, `tolower`, `_Unwind_*`, `__cxa_*`, ...).

## Test coverage of the exported surface

Of the 143 exported symbols, **134 are called directly** by the differential
tests through `libloading` (see `tests/common/mod.rs`, which resolves each one by
its exact linker name — so a missing or misnamed export fails at load time).

The remaining 9 take a pointer to the compiler's internal `compile_block`, which
cannot be constructed correctly from outside the library, so they are exercised
**transitively**:

| symbol | reached via |
|---|---|
| `_pcre2_auto_possessify_8` | `pcre2_compile_8` (unless `PCRE2_NO_AUTO_POSSESS`) |
| `_pcre2_check_escape_8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for every `\`-escape |
| `_pcre2_compile_class_nested_8` | `pcre2_compile_8` with `PCRE2_ALT_EXTENDED_CLASS` |
| `_pcre2_compile_class_not_nested_8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for every character class |
| `_pcre2_compile_add_name_to_table8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for every named group |
| `_pcre2_compile_find_named_group8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for every name reference |
| `_pcre2_compile_find_dupname_details8` | `pcre2_compile_8` with `PCRE2_DUPNAMES` |
| `_pcre2_compile_parse_recurse_args8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for `(?&name)` / `(?1)` |
| `_pcre2_compile_parse_scan_substr_args8` | `pcre2_compile_8` for `(*scs:…)` |

Transitive coverage is strong here rather than nominal: every compile in the
suite is checked by **byte-comparing the entire compiled bytecode** (via
`pcre2_serialize_encode_8`) between the two libraries, across a 200-pattern
corpus × 26 option axes plus ~19 000 randomized/fuzzed patterns. Any divergence
inside these nine functions changes the generated bytecode and fails the
comparison. The dedicated class/name/recursion patterns in
`tests/compile_match.rs` and `tests/compile_errors.rs` target each of them.

## Symbol type legend

`T` = code (text), `R` = read-only data, `D` = initialised data, `B` = bss.
